title: First Trimester Nutrition Checklist: Folate, Iron, and Safer Foods
excerpt: Prioritize folic acid, iron-rich foods, hydration, and cooked foods during weeks 1-12
content:
## Introduction
During the first trimester of pregnancy, nutrition plays a crucial role in supporting the development of the fetus. Providing adequate essential nutrients will help both the mother and the fetus stay healthy. In this article, we will explore the key factors in first-trimester nutrition, including folate, iron, and safer foods.

## Folate and its importance
Folate is a crucial nutrient during pregnancy, especially during the first trimester. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), folate helps prevent neural tube defects in the fetus. Pregnant women should consume 400-800 micrograms of folate daily. Foods rich in folate include leafy greens, fruits, and dairy products.

## Iron and its role
Iron is another essential nutrient during pregnancy. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), iron helps support the development of the fetus and prevents anemia in pregnant women. Pregnant women should consume 27 milligrams of iron daily. Foods rich in iron include red meat, chicken, fish, and legumes.

## Safer foods
During the first trimester of pregnancy, pregnant women should prioritize safer foods to avoid the risk of food poisoning. According to the National Health Service (NHS), pregnant women should avoid undercooked foods, such as sushi, sashimi, and raw eggs. Instead, they should opt for cooked foods, such as cooked meat, fish, and vegetables.

## Sample meal plan
Here are some sample meal ideas for pregnant women during the first trimester:
* Breakfast: Oatmeal with fruit and milk
* Lunch: Cooked chicken with steamed vegetables and brown rice
* Dinner: Grilled fish with roasted vegetables and quinoa

## Conclusion
First-trimester nutrition is crucial for supporting the development of the fetus. Pregnant women should prioritize folate, iron, and safer foods to ensure the health of both mother and fetus. For more information on pregnancy nutrition, pregnant women can visit [our website](/planner) or [read more about related topics](/blog/topics).

## When to seek help
If pregnant women have any questions or concerns about pregnancy nutrition, they should consult their doctor or a registered dietitian for advice.
